newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina hopes job protests will end in Jujuy.
newsitem.headline: Argentina hopes job protests will end in Jujuy.

text.p: The Argentine government was hopeful on Friday that roadblock protests against unemployment in the poor northwestern province of Jujuy would be lifted after it pledged 10,000 new jobs.
Church and union leaders were negotiating an end to the roadblocks in the province, where well over 100 people were hurt in clashes between police and protesters last week.

"There are structural problems that cannot be solved like magic overnight but the tense situation of recent days will calm down and the roadblocks will probably be lifted," Deputy Interior Minister Alberto Iribarne said.

Violent police action against shanty dwellers blocking a highway in Jujuy last week sparked more than 20 similar protests across the mountainous province and a handful of roadblocks further south in the province of Cordoba.

The wave of protest against unemployment exceeding 17 percent started in April among teachers and oil workers in Patagonia and spread to Salta and Jujuy in the northwest and the central province of Cordoba, where jobless farmhands lifted their barricade on Friday.

Police use of tear gas and rubber bullets has drawn warnings from the Roman Catholic Church and the International Monetary Fund, which recommended many of the orthodox economic reforms that President Carlos Menem has applied successfully since coming to power in 1989.
"The IMF has more social sensitivity than President Menem. What the government has not spent on food it has spent on bullets," opposition Radical Party leader Rodolfo Terragno said.
Amnesty International said it had written to Menem expressing concern about "the apparent use of excessive force" by police and paramilitary police.

After two weeks' rioting in Jujuy, student protests in Buenos Aires and nearby La Plata and trouble in such other cities as Cordoba and Mendoza, the Peronist government offered Jujuy 10,000 low-paid, short-term jobs.
Since some sugar and steel towns in the province are experiencing unemployment of up to 37 percent, the offer was being seriously considered.
